entries.title: The great tree
entries.summary: The island's only tree gives branches, limbs, leaves, twigs and seeds, and regrows what you take as fast as sunlight, water and nutrients allow. Felling it is a big decision.

sections.text: The tree is alive, and it grows only one way: by taking carbon from the island's air, and water and nutrients from the soil within about three meters of its trunk. What it makes goes into a reserve first, and from there into new branches, new limbs and a thicker trunk.

Its eight small branches can be cut with a blade or an axe: aim at one and hold [key]LMB[/key]. After a few strokes the leafy branch drops to the ground. A cut branch grows back from the tree's reserve - in about ten in-game hours at best. Until then it shows as a young branch, with how far it has grown, and it can't be cut.

The five big limbs need an axe: hold [key]LMB[/key] on one, and it takes a good number of blows. A large limb is heavy and full of useful wood (see [b]Working wood[/b]). Limbs grow back too, more slowly: a day at the very least.
When it has reserves to spare, the tree lets fall a twig every several hours, a handful of leaves about once a day and a winged seed every day or so. Look around its foot.

list: Don't strip it all at once: with few leaves the tree makes little.
Keep the soil around it moist in dry weather. Water and compost around its roots both help.
It doesn't grow at night, and grows slowly in cold, cloudy weather.

sections.text: With an axe you can fell the trunk itself: around thirty blows with a good axe, more with a poor one. It creaks when it's nearly through. It comes down as two great logs, a couple of limbs and some firewood, along with every full-grown branch and limb that was still on it.

The roots survive the felling. From their stored reserves the stump pushes up a sapling, which - given sun, water and nutrients - becomes a young tree and then a full tree again. That takes days, and until it is grown there are no branches to cut.

sections.warn: Felling the tree trades a steady, regrowing supply of branches and limbs for one load of logs. Make sure you need those boards before you do it.

sections.text: Hold a tree seed and press [key]RMB[/key] on any soil - no tilling needed - at least two and a half meters from other plants and trees. A seedling starts from almost nothing and grows slowly; water it in dry weather.

entries.title: Working wood
entries.summary: Cut branches into sticks and twigs, chop limbs into poles and firewood, carve hearth boards, and split logs into boards - careful splits for boards, quick ones for firewood.

sections.text: Wood is worked where it lies. Set the piece on the ground ([key]RMB[/key]), hold the right tool and hold [key]LMB[/key] on it; after a few strokes it comes apart into smaller things. Bark, crumbs and chips aren't wasted - they go back into the soil where you worked.

list: [b]Leafy branch[/b] (blade or axe): 2 sticks, 3 twigs and a handful of leaves.
[b]Large limb[/b] (axe): 2 poles, 3 sticks, 2 firewood, 2 twigs and 2 handfuls of leaves.
[b]Stick[/b] (blade or axe): carved into a hearth board for the fire drill.

sections.text: Logs and big split pieces need an axe, and you split them with single, aimed blows of [key]LMB[/key] on the end. The wood splits along the line you strike: aim at the middle to halve it, nearer one side to take off a slab. A poor axe sometimes just bites in without splitting.

What a split piece becomes depends on its shape. A slab about 2 to 7.5 centimeters thick and at least 15 centimeters wide becomes rough boards, with the offcuts as firewood. Anything small - under about 6 kilograms - becomes firewood. Everything else stays a half log, a slab or a piece of split wood, ready to be split again.
steps: Split the log down the middle into two half logs.
Take slabs off each half by striking close to one side.
Split any slab that is still too thick until it comes apart into boards.

sections.text: Poles - long and straight - come only from limbs, and they are the backbone of every building. Sticks come from branches and limbs: handles, spindles, wattle rods and kindling.
Everything cut from the tree starts out green. Lay it out in sun and wind for a day or two before you burn it or stack it into a charcoal mound.

sections.tip: Platforms and shelves are built from boards, and boards only come from logs. Split carefully: a patient splitter gets several boards out of each log, and the offcuts still make firewood.
